title: Cutting the cost of cooking
paragraphs: Are you planning to eat out tonight or are you going to stay in to save the pennies? A meal out at a good restaurant or even a pizza parlour can set you back a small fortune, so cooking for yourself makes financial sense. But with the rise in food prices, it's important to be a savvy shopper to keep your food bill in check.

These days our supermarket shelves are packed with a tempting array of food items: from the daily staples, like bread and milk, to the exotic, like mangoes and saffron. There's also the option of buying ready meals – convenient food that comes at a price. However, if you're feeling the pinch, there are things you can do to make the money you spend on food go further.

According to the BBC Food website, it's all about changing your habits. It claims that cooking filling and tasty meals on a budget is easy. It suggests a number of 'tricks' such as using cheaper cuts of meat, "bulk out small amounts of meat with less expensive proteins" and "transform small amounts of leftovers into a filling meal".

A favourite pastime of mine to help when money is tight is to stock up on items that are on special offer – such as BOGOF deals (Buy one, get one free). However, this is more of a problem when it comes to perishable items like fresh fruit and vegetables. In the UK, about 39% of household food waste is fruit and veg. So it's a good idea not to stock up on too much of these things. Store them carefully and make the most of them in all your recipes.

Food waste is a big problem generally so shopping carefully can also reduce the amount we throw away. And in Edinburgh in Scotland, it's possible to reduce waste and not break the bank by visiting a recycled food shop, which has been set up to prevent surplus food from shops ending up in the bin. The Food Sharing Hub allows people to pay as much as they want for the rescued food, which is past its 'best before date'.
Of course, the biggest thing you can do to help your cash flow is to cut back on takeaway coffees and lunches. Making your own is usually healthier for you and your finances!

vocabulary.entry: save the pennies /seɪv ðə ˈpeniz/ 省钱；精打细算
vocabulary.example: I'm saving the pennies for a new laptop.
vocabulary.translation: 我正在省钱想买一台新笔记本电脑。

vocabulary.term: set you back a small fortune
vocabulary.entry: set you back a small fortune /set juː bæk ə smɔːl ˈfɔːtʃuːn/ 花掉你一小笔钱
vocabulary.example: That designer dress will set you back a small fortune.
vocabulary.translation: 那条名牌连衣裙会花掉你一小笔钱。

vocabulary.entry: make financial sense /meɪk faɪˈnænʃl sens/ 具有经济意义；从经济角度看是明智的
vocabulary.example: Buying a used car makes financial sense for new drivers.
vocabulary.translation: 对新手司机来说，买二手车在经济上是明智的选择。

vocabulary.entry: savvy shopper /ˈsævi ˈʃɒpə(r)/ 精明的购物者
vocabulary.example: A savvy shopper always compares prices before buying.
vocabulary.translation: 精明的购物者在购买前总会货比三家。

vocabulary.entry: keep...in check /kiːp ɪn tʃek/ 控制；约束
vocabulary.example: We need to keep our spending in check during the economic downturn.
vocabulary.translation: 经济下行期间，我们需要控制开支。

vocabulary.entry: a tempting array of /ə ˈtemptɪŋ əˈreɪ ɒv/ 一系列诱人的
vocabulary.example: The shop window displays a tempting array of chocolates.
vocabulary.translation: 商店橱窗里陈列着一系列诱人的巧克力。

vocabulary.entry: daily staples /ˈdeɪli ˈsteɪplz/ 日常主食（复数）
vocabulary.example: Rice and noodles are daily staples in many Asian countries.
vocabulary.translation: 大米和面条是许多亚洲国家的日常主食。

vocabulary.entry: exotic /ɪɡˈzɒtɪk/ adj. 异国风味的；外来的
vocabulary.example: The restaurant serves exotic dishes from Southeast Asia.
vocabulary.translation: 这家餐厅供应东南亚的异国风味菜肴。

vocabulary.entry: ready meals /ˈredi miːlz/ 即食餐；预制餐（复数）
vocabulary.example: Ready meals are popular among busy office workers.
vocabulary.translation: 即食餐很受忙碌的上班族欢迎。

vocabulary.entry: feel the pinch /fiːl ðə pɪntʃ/ 手头拮据；感到经济困难
vocabulary.example: Many families are feeling the pinch due to rising inflation.
vocabulary.translation: 由于通货膨胀加剧，许多家庭都感到手头拮据。

vocabulary.entry: make...go further /meɪk ɡəʊ ˈfɜːðə(r)/ 让……更耐用；让……花得更值
vocabulary.example: Using coupons can make your money go further when shopping.
vocabulary.translation: 购物时使用优惠券能让你的钱花得更值。

vocabulary.entry: on a budget /ɒn ə ˈbʌdʒɪt/ 节省开支；预算有限
vocabulary.example: We are traveling on a budget, so we choose cheap hotels.
vocabulary.translation: 我们旅行预算有限，所以会选择便宜的酒店。

vocabulary.entry: cheaper cuts of meat /ˈtʃiːpə kʌts ɒv miːt/ 价格实惠的肉块（复数）
vocabulary.example: Slow cooking is perfect for cheaper cuts of meat.
vocabulary.translation: 慢炖很适合烹饪价格实惠的肉块。

vocabulary.entry: bulk out /bʌlk aʊt/ 使……分量增加
vocabulary.example: We can bulk out the soup with potatoes and carrots.
vocabulary.translation: 我们可以加土豆和胡萝卜让汤的分量更足。

vocabulary.entry: leftovers /ˈleftəʊvəz/ n. 剩菜剩饭（复数）
vocabulary.example: We had leftovers for lunch the next day.
vocabulary.translation: 第二天我们用剩菜剩饭当午餐。

vocabulary.entry: stock up on /stɒk ʌp ɒn/ 大量购买；囤购
vocabulary.example: People usually stock up on food before a storm.
vocabulary.translation: 人们通常会在暴风雨来临前囤购食物。

vocabulary.entry: BOGOF (Buy one, get one free) /ˌbiː əʊ dʒiː əʊ ˈef/ 买一送一（促销活动）
vocabulary.example: The supermarket has a BOGOF offer on bottled water this week.
vocabulary.translation: 这家超市这周瓶装水有买一送一的优惠。

vocabulary.entry: perishable /ˈperɪʃəbl/ adj. 易腐烂的
vocabulary.example: Perishable goods like milk need to be stored in the fridge.
vocabulary.translation: 牛奶之类的易腐烂商品需要放在冰箱里储存。

vocabulary.entry: surplus food /ˈsɜːpləs fuːd/ 过剩食品
vocabulary.example: The charity distributes surplus food to the homeless.
vocabulary.translation: 这家慈善机构向无家可归者分发过剩食品。

vocabulary.entry: best before date /best bɪˈfɔː deɪt/ 最佳食用日期
vocabulary.example: You'd better eat the yogurt before its best before date.
vocabulary.translation: 你最好在最佳食用日期前吃掉这份酸奶。

vocabulary.entry: cash flow /kæʃ fləʊ/ 资金流动；现金流
vocabulary.example: The small business is having cash flow problems.
vocabulary.translation: 这家小企业正面临现金流问题。

vocabulary.entry: cut back on /kʌt bæk ɒn/ 减少；削减
vocabulary.example: I need to cut back on my sugar intake to stay healthy.
vocabulary.translation: 为了保持健康，我需要减少糖分摄入。

sentences.english: Are you planning to eat out tonight or are you going to stay in to save the pennies?
sentences.chinese: 你今晚打算出去吃饭，还是为了省钱在家做饭？

sentences.english: A meal out at a good restaurant or even a pizza parlour can set you back a small fortune, so cooking for yourself makes financial sense.
sentences.chinese: 在一家不错的餐厅甚至披萨店吃一顿，都可能让你花掉一小笔钱，所以自己做饭从经济角度来说是明智的。

sentences.english: But with the rise in food prices, it's important to be a savvy shopper to keep your food bill in check.
sentences.chinese: 但随着食品价格上涨，做个精明的购物者来控制食品开支就显得尤为重要。

sentences.english: These days our supermarket shelves are packed with a tempting array of food items: from the daily staples, like bread and milk, to the exotic, like mangoes and saffron.
sentences.chinese: 如今，超市货架上摆满了琳琅满目的诱人食品：从面包、牛奶这类日常主食，到芒果、藏红花之类的异国风味食材，应有尽有。

sentences.english: There's also the option of buying ready meals – convenient food that comes at a price.
sentences.chinese: 你也可以选择购买即食餐——这种食品虽然方便，但价格不菲。

sentences.english: However, if you're feeling the pinch, there are things you can do to make the money you spend on food go further.
sentences.chinese: 不过，如果你手头拮据，还是有一些办法能让你花在食物上的钱更划算。

sentences.english: According to the BBC Food website, it's all about changing your habits.
sentences.chinese: 据英国广播公司美食频道网站称，关键在于改变你的习惯。

sentences.english: It claims that cooking filling and tasty meals on a budget is easy.
sentences.chinese: 该网站称，低成本做出既饱腹又美味的饭菜并非难事。

sentences.english: It suggests a number of 'tricks' such as using cheaper cuts of meat, "bulk out small amounts of meat with less expensive proteins" and "transform small amounts of leftovers into a filling meal".
sentences.chinese: 网站还给出了不少“小窍门”，比如选用价格实惠的肉块、“用廉价蛋白质食材来搭配少量肉类做成一顿大餐”，以及“把少量剩菜剩饭做成一顿管饱的正餐”。

sentences.english: A favourite pastime of mine to help when money is tight is to stock up on items that are on special offer – such as BOGOF deals (Buy one, get one free).
sentences.chinese: 当手头紧的时候，我最喜欢的娱乐消遣省钱活动就是囤购特价商品——比如“买一送一”的优惠活动。

sentences.english: However, this is more of a problem when it comes to perishable items like fresh fruit and vegetables.
sentences.chinese: 但这种方法对于新鲜水果、蔬菜这类易腐烂食材来说，就不太适用了。

sentences.english: In the UK, about 39% of household food waste is fruit and veg.
sentences.chinese: 在英国，约39%的家庭食物垃圾都是果蔬类。

sentences.english: So it's a good idea not to stock up on too much of these things.
sentences.chinese: 所以，这类食材最好不要囤太多。

sentences.english: Store them carefully and make the most of them in all your recipes.
sentences.chinese: 要妥善储存，并在各种食谱中充分利用它们。

sentences.english: Food waste is a big problem generally so shopping carefully can also reduce the amount we throw away.
sentences.chinese: 食物浪费是一个普遍存在的大问题，因此谨慎购物也能减少我们丢弃的食物量。

sentences.english: And in Edinburgh in Scotland, it's possible to reduce waste and not break the bank by visiting a recycled food shop, which has been set up to prevent surplus food from shops ending up in the bin.
sentences.chinese: 在苏格兰的爱丁堡，你可以光顾一家食品循环回收商店，既能减少浪费，又不会花太多钱。这家商店的设立是为了避免商店的过剩食品被扔进垃圾桶。

sentences.english: The Food Sharing Hub allows people to pay as much as they want for the rescued food, which is past its 'best before date'.
sentences.chinese: 这家名为“食品共享中心”的商店允许人们想付多少就付多少来购买那些已过“最佳食用日期”的回收食品。

sentences.english: Of course, the biggest thing you can do to help your cash flow is to cut back on takeaway coffees and lunches.
sentences.chinese: 当然，要改善资金状况，最有效的办法就是减少购买外卖咖啡和午餐的次数。

sentences.english: Making your own is usually healthier for you and your finances!
sentences.chinese: 自己动手做，通常对你的健康和钱包都更有益！
